To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of inflammation‐related molecules in AT is modulated in response to weight loss, that the modulation of these genes is not uniform and that some genes may be used to monitor the success of weight loss treatments.
obesity and weight loss are accompanied by specific changes in the AT gene expression profile, and that these changes are associated with a low‐grade inflammation in obese subjects.

(i) AT is an active tissue that responds to environmental changes by modulating gene expression, (ii) obesity is a chronic inflammation‐associated disease, and (iii) AT gene expression changes are reversible and may be used for the identification of new targets for therapeutic intervention.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of biomarkers of inflammation in human AT, and the understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying their regulation.
the identification of biomarkers of inflammation and the development of new therapeutic strategies in obesity.
the identification of new biomarkers of obesity‐related inflammation.

the inflammatory status in AT is a dynamic process, and that the identification of specific markers of obesity‐related inflammation is of major interest.
